scope.flow: Token graduation via launchpad.buy() triggering _createPairAndSwapRemaining and createPair
scope.environment: GTE Launchpad V2 (Launchpad.sol, GTELaunchpadV2PairFactory.sol) on EVM with public mempool

statements.text: The createPair function of GTELaunchpadV2PairFactory.sol is publicly callable by anyone for any two tokens.
The factory enables the launchpad fee-on-transfer mechanism only when msg.sender of createPair is the Launchpad contract; any other caller gets a standard fee-less pair.
The attacker can observe the mempool for a launchpad.buy() transaction that will graduate a new token.
A token's bonding curve is fully sold, so the final buy transaction triggers _createPairAndSwapRemaining.
The try/catch around createPair in _createPairAndSwapRemaining has an empty catch block that swallows the PAIR_EXISTS revert.
The attacker submits a factory.createPair() transaction for the same token pair with a higher gas fee.
The attacker's createPair transaction is mined first, creating a standard Uniswap pair without the GTE fee mechanism.
The legitimate launchpad.buy() transaction is then mined and its internal createPair call fails.
The empty catch block swallows the PAIR_EXISTS revert, so execution continues in a broken state and the graduation transaction reverts when uniV2Router.addLiquidity fails.
The legitimate launchpad.buy() graduation transaction reverts because the pair already exists and the graduation logic cannot handle that state.
The token can never graduate, its liquidity pool can never be seeded by the protocol, and its transfers can never be unlocked.
Creating the pair without the launchpad as originator permanently prevents the GTE fee-on-transfer mechanism from being attached to that token's pair.

A token whose bonding curve is fully sold should be able to complete graduation: the launchpad's createPair call should succeed and seed the pair with the GTE fee mechanism, rather than being blocked by a pre-existing pair.
The attacker is able to get their createPair transaction mined before the legitimate graduation transaction by paying a higher gas fee.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether the attacker's createPair call is permissionless in practice beyond the factory being publicly callable.
Report does not specify the exact token pair or whether the attacker needs to hold any tokens to call createPair.
Report does not establish that a real front-running incident was observed; the scenario is described as possible.
Report does not state whether the legitimate buy transaction's revert is guaranteed or only occurs under the described ordering.
